clock_quality.rule: Per-row clock_quality. published rows: available_utc is realtime_start + 1 day 00:00 UTC (available_rule next_day_00utc), or the series' first ALFRED vintage + 1 day for pre-tracking history (first_vintage_next_day_00utc; a lower bound, not a publication instant). unvintaged rows (available_rule vintage_precedes_observation): FRED's vintage date precedes the observation period, no credible availability instant, available_utc null.

name: alfred_vintages
notes: Method: FRED series/observations with output_type=1 (observations by real-time period) over the full real-time range 1776-07-04..9999-12-31, split into windows of at most 1500 vintage dates (API limit 2000) at series/vintagedates boundaries; periods clipped at a window edge are merged with their continuation (same date, same value, adjacent days). Verified live 2026-09-15 that FRED clips periods at the requested window and never emits adjacent equal-valued periods in an unwindowed response.
observation_start=2009-01-01 (one year before the 2010 target so 2010 year-over-year rates are computable); every vintage since the first ALFRED vintage is included.
Rows whose FRED value is '.' (no observation, e.g. market holidays for daily series) are dropped; per-series counts are in series_stats.

available_utc: FRED states no release time-of-day for any of these series (series notes checked live 2026-09-15). Rule next_day_00utc: realtime_start + 1 day at 00:00 UTC, the conservative end of the vintage's civil day (ALFRED vintage dates are US civil dates; these publishers release during US business hours). Rule first_vintage_next_day_00utc: observations whose period ended before the series' first ALFRED vintage are reported by FRED with realtime_start at that first vintage (DEXCHUS: at the series' 2005-06-28 FRED inception), which proves the value current then but says nothing about first publication; available_utc = first vintage + 1 day, a safe lower bound. Rule vintage_precedes_observation: FRED's realtime_start lies before the observation period end although the series was tracked (e.g. VIXCLS values dated a US holiday carried in the prior business day's vintage; DCOILWTICO/DCOILBRENTEU 2012-12-27 in the 2012-12-26 vintage); FRED's own as-of query confirms this and no credible availability time exists, so clock_quality = unvintaged and available_utc = null. FRED fields are never altered.

Vintage semantics proof: PAYEMS observation 2026-08-01 first appears with realtime_start 2026-09-04 (the BLS Employment Situation release for August 2026); the proof-PAYEMS-asof-* captures show the observation absent as of 2026-09-03 and present as of 2026-09-04.
All 32 requested series exist in ALFRED; none skipped.
